content:
- When sentiment is consistently bullish (positive) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecasted peaks, especially in early 30d horizon.
- When sentiment is bearish (negative) or mixed, model often underestimates downside risk; increase downward bias in forecast, especially if recent price is trending up.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1-2 days), leading to overshoot in 30d forecast; cap or smooth out sharp upward moves.
- If sentiment flips from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; introduce a “sentiment pivot” rule: if sentiment changes direction within 7-10 days, reduce forecast slope or shift mean toward prior 14-day average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon; if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 14-day mean, reduce by 10-20% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Model underestimates late-period spikes (especially >65) when sentiment is bullish; add a “late horizon bias” rule: if sentiment >0.7 for last 5 days, increase forecast by 0.5-1.0σ in final 7-10 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often fails to capture volatility; increase forecast variance (±0.5-1.0σ) around mean to reflect uncertainty.
